The number of salts from the given list that are coloured in their solid state is ____.

$\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{FeSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{NiSO}_4 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{ZnSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$, $\text{BaCl}_2 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2$
The number of salts from the given list that are coloured in their solid state is ____.
questions.solution:
The colour of transition metal salts is generally due to d-d transitions, which require partially filled d-orbitals.

$\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($3d^9$), which has one unpaired electron and is blue in colour.

$\text{FeSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6$), which has four unpaired electrons and is pale green in colour.

$\text{NiSO}_4 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3d^8$), which has two unpaired electrons and is green in colour.

$\text{ZnSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($3d^{10}$), which has a completely filled d-subshell and is colourless (white).

$\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ contains $\text{Al}^{3+}$, which has no d-electrons and is colourless (white).

$\text{BaCl}_2 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, an alkaline earth metal ion with no d-electrons, and is colourless (white).

$\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2$ contains $\text{Pb}^{2+}$, a p-block ion with a completely filled d-subshell, and is colourless (white).

Thus, there are 3 coloured salts in the given list.

Answer: $3$

questions.question: An inorganic salt on dry heating in a test tube evolves a colourless and odourless gas, and leaves behind a residue which is yellow when hot and white when cold. The salt is:
questions.solution:
When zinc carbonate is heated, it undergoes thermal decomposition to form zinc oxide and carbon dioxide gas.

$\text{ZnCO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{ZnO} + \text{CO}_2 \uparrow$

The evolved gas, carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$), is colourless and odourless.

The residue left behind is zinc oxide ($\text{ZnO}$), which exhibits a characteristic property of being yellow when hot and white when cold due to the creation of non-stoichiometric defects at high temperatures.

Other options:
$\text{CuCO}_3$ leaves a black residue of $\text{CuO}$.
$\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2$ evolves brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas.
$\text{CaCO}_3$ leaves a white residue of $\text{CaO}$ which remains white when hot or cold.

Answer: $\text{ZnCO}_3$

questions.solution:
In a dry flame test, different metal cations impart characteristic colours to the flame due to the excitation and subsequent emission of electrons.

$\text{Ca}^{2+}$ imparts a brick red colour to the flame.

$\text{Ba}^{2+}$ imparts an apple green colour to the flame.

$\text{Mg}^{2+}$ does not impart any characteristic colour to the flame because the energy required to excite its valence electrons is very high.

$\text{Cu}^{2+}$ imparts a blue-green colour to the flame.

Therefore, $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ is correctly matched with apple green.

Answer: $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ : Apple green

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the borax bead test, the transparent glassy bead formed on heating borax is composed of sodium metaborate and boric anhydride.
Statement II: The borax bead test is generally applicable to coloured salts of transition metals.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the borax bead test, the transparent glassy bead formed on heating borax is composed of sodium metaborate and boric anhydride.
Statement II: The borax bead test is generally applicable to coloured salts of transition metals.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Borax on heating loses water of crystallization to form anhydrous borax, which on further heating melts to form a transparent glassy bead. This bead is a mixture of sodium metaborate and boric anhydride.

$Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O \xrightarrow{\Delta} Na_2B_4O_7 + 10H_2O$

$Na_2B_4O_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2NaBO_2 + B_2O_3$

Thus, Statement I is correct.

The borax bead test is used for the detection of transition metals because they form characteristically coloured metaborates when heated with the glassy bead. For example, cobalt forms a blue bead of $Co(BO_2)_2$.

Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.question: During the borax bead test of a copper salt, the bead obtained after heating in a luminous (reducing) flame is red and opaque when cold. If this red opaque bead is subsequently reheated in a non-luminous (oxidising) flame and allowed to cool, it:
options: remains red, because the reduction to elemental copper is irreversible under flame conditions.
becomes colourless, due to the formation of cuprous metaborate, $\text{CuBO}_2$.
turns black, due to the decomposition of the bead to form cupric oxide, $\text{CuO}$.
turns blue, due to the oxidation of the copper species to cupric metaborate, $\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$.
questions.solution:
In the borax bead test, heating a copper salt in a reducing (luminous) flame reduces the copper species to elemental copper or cuprous oxide, which makes the bead red and opaque when cold.

The reactions in the reducing flame are:
$2\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2 + \text{C} \rightarrow 2\text{CuBO}_2 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{CO}$
$2\text{CuBO}_2 + \text{C} \rightarrow 2\text{Cu} + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{CO}$

When this red opaque bead is reheated in an oxidising (non-luminous) flame, the elemental copper is oxidised back to the cupric state ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$), forming cupric metaborate.

The reactions in the oxidising flame are:
$2\text{Cu} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CuO}$
$\text{CuO} + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$

Cupric metaborate, $\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$, imparts a characteristic blue colour to the bead when cold.

Answer: turns blue, due to the oxidation of the copper species to cupric metaborate, $\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$.

questions.question: A metal ion produces a reddish-brown borax bead in a cold oxidising flame. When heated in a reducing flame, the bead becomes grey and opaque. The metal ion is:
questions.solution:
In the borax bead test, nickel salts produce a reddish-brown bead in a cold oxidising flame due to the formation of nickel(II) metaborate, $\text{Ni(BO}_2\text{)}_2$.

In a reducing flame, the bead becomes grey and opaque due to the reduction of nickel metaborate to finely divided metallic nickel.

For comparison:
$\text{Cu}^{2+}$ gives a blue bead in a cold oxidising flame and a red opaque bead in a cold reducing flame.
$\text{Fe}^{3+}$ gives a yellow bead in a cold oxidising flame and a green bead in a reducing flame.
$\text{Zn}^{2+}$ gives a colourless bead.

Therefore, the metal ion is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$.

Answer: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$

Answer: $\text{CoAl}_2\text{O}_4$

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, $\text{NaHCO}_3$, $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$, and $\text{KHCO}_3$
An aqueous $\text{MgSO}_4$ solution is added to each of these salt solutions at room temperature without heating. The number of salt solutions that produce a white precipitate under these conditions is ____.
questions.solution:
When an aqueous solution of $\text{MgSO}_4$ is added to soluble carbonates at room temperature, a white precipitate of magnesium carbonate (or basic magnesium carbonate) is formed.

$\text{MgSO}_4 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgCO}_3 \downarrow + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$

$\text{MgSO}_4 + \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgCO}_3 \downarrow + \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$

When $\text{MgSO}_4$ is added to soluble bicarbonates at room temperature, magnesium bicarbonate is formed, which is soluble in water. Thus, no precipitate is observed without heating.

$\text{MgSO}_4 + 2\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2 \text{ (soluble)} + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$

$\text{MgSO}_4 + 2\text{KHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2 \text{ (soluble)} + \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$

Therefore, only $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ and $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ produce a white precipitate under the given conditions. The number of such solutions is $2$.

Answer: $2$

(i) the gas turns filter paper moistened with lead acetate solution into a black compound 'P'.

(i) the gas turns filter paper moistened with lead acetate solution into a black compound 'P'.
(ii) adding sodium nitroprusside to the alkaline sodium carbonate extract of the salt yields a violet-coloured complex anion 'Q'.

The chemical formula of compound 'P' and the net charge on the complex anion 'Q' are, respectively:
questions.solution:
The gas with the smell of rotten eggs evolved on treating the salt with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is hydrogen sulfide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$), indicating the presence of sulfide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) ions.

$\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas reacts with lead acetate to form a black precipitate of lead sulfide ($\text{PbS}$).

$\text{Pb}(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2 + \text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow \text{PbS} + 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$

Thus, the black compound 'P' is $\text{PbS}$.

Sulfide ions react with sodium nitroprusside in an alkaline medium to form a violet-coloured complex, sodium thionitroprusside.

$\text{S}^{2-} + [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NO}]^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$

The violet-coloured complex anion 'Q' is $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$, which has a net charge of $-4$.

Therefore, 'P' is $\text{PbS}$ and the net charge on 'Q' is $-4$.

Answer: $\text{PbS}$ and $-4$

questions.question: During the systematic analysis of an inorganic salt, the presence of sulphide ions in the sodium carbonate extract is confirmed by adding lead acetate solution. The extract is first acidified with dilute acetic acid. Dilute sulphuric acid is not used for this acidification because:
options: it oxidises the sulphide ions to elemental sulphur, preventing the formation of black $\text{PbS}$.
it introduces sulphate ions which form a white precipitate of $\text{PbSO}_4$, interfering with the test.
it reduces the lead(II) ions of the reagent to metallic lead.
it reacts with lead acetate to evolve pungent sulphur dioxide gas.
questions.solution:
The sodium carbonate extract is alkaline and needs to be acidified before adding lead acetate to test for sulphide ions.

If dilute sulphuric acid is used for acidification, it introduces sulphate ions ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) into the solution.

When lead acetate is added, the lead(II) ions ($\text{Pb}^{2+}$) react with the sulphate ions to form a white precipitate of lead sulphate ($\text{PbSO}_4$).

$\text{Pb}^{2+} + \text{SO}_4^{2-} \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4 \downarrow \text{ (white precipitate)}$

This white precipitate interferes with the detection of the black precipitate of lead sulphide ($\text{PbS}$), which is the positive result for the sulphide test.

Therefore, dilute acetic acid is used instead, as lead acetate is soluble and does not form a precipitate with acetate ions.

Answer: it introduces sulphate ions which form a white precipitate of $\text{PbSO}_4$, interfering with the test.

The chromyl chloride test involves heating a chloride salt with solid potassium dichromate and concentrated sulfuric acid to evolve reddish-brown vapours of chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$).

Answer: $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$

Thus, $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ is the correct cation.

The white gelatinous precipitate of $\text{Al(OH)}_3$ is amphoteric and dissolves in excess $\text{NaOH}$ to form a soluble complex, sodium aluminate.

$\text{Al(OH)}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}[\text{Al(OH)}_4]$ (soluble)

Thus, the salt 'X' is $\text{AlCl}_3$.

Answer: $\text{AlCl}_3$

Before the end point, the added $\text{KMnO}_4$ is continuously reduced to colourless $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ions. At the end point, the addition of a single drop of $\text{KMnO}_4$ in excess imparts a permanent light pink colour to the solution.

Thus, the colour changes from colourless to light pink.

Answer: $\text{KMnO}_4$ acts as a self-indicator; the colour changes from colourless to light pink
